# REAL LIFE RPG — HYBRID GAP-CLOSURE GUIDE (coding agent)

Stack: plain HTML, CSS, JS, Jinja2 templates. No React. This extends the existing `garden-rpg` theme — keep its file structure, tokens, and layout skeleton. This is not a rebuild.

**Image assets are NOT generated by you.** The user generates them separately with an AI image tool and drops them into the exact folders/filenames below. You do not have image generation capability and must not attempt to fake, draw, or synthesize these images yourself. Every image reference in this guide MUST be implemented with a placeholder fallback (Stage 0 below) so the page looks correct and finished even when zero real art files exist yet. Treat "no image file present" as the expected default state during development, not an error case.

---

## The one rule everything else follows

**USER ACTION → RPG PROGRESSION → ATTRIBUTE CHANGE → WORLD CHANGE**, and it has to be visible, not implied. Every attribute (INT/STA/FCS/CHA/DSC) owns a region of the garden, every region has 4 tiers tied to that attribute's value, and completing a mission must show its effect traveling from the task to the attribute to the region.

**Do not:**
- Split the screen into "Garden side" + "Command Centre side." The garden stays the central visual anchor; HUD panels wrap around it.
- Make the garden a static `<img>` with floating labels. It's a stateful component driven by attribute data (Stage 1).
- Use green as a generic "success" color everywhere. Green is DSC's color only.
- Duplicate navigation. One nav system (Stage 2).
- Assume an image file exists before checking for it. Every `<img>` this guide describes must go through the placeholder system in Stage 0 first.

---

## Data model additions (do this first)

Extend the context dict from the base theme guide's Section 13:

```python
regions = {
  "academy": {"attr": "int", "value": 72, "tier": <computed 1-4 from value>, "name": "Academy"},
  "river":   {"attr": "sta", "value": 81, "tier": ..., "name": "River"},
  "moon":    {"attr": "fcs", "value": 68, "tier": ..., "name": "Moon"},
  "village": {"attr": "cha", "value": 63, "tier": ..., "name": "Village"},
}
# DSC does not get its own region — see garden_health below.

garden_health = {"discipline": 78, "state": "FLOURISHING"}  # FLOURISHING / STABLE / NEGLECTED

player = {
  "title": "Wayfarer", "next_title": "Pathfinder",
  "garden_name": "Kim's Garden",
  "day": 42, "season": "SPRING", "time_of_day": "EVENING",
}

missions = [
  {"id": "mission-1", "tag": "MAIN", "title": "Study Control Systems",
   "status": "ACTIVE",  # AVAILABLE/ACTIVE/COMPLETED/COMPLETED_LATE/MISSED/ABANDONED/RESCHEDULED/LOCKED
   "difficulty": 3, "attr_deltas": {"int": 3, "fcs": 1, "dsc": 1},
   "xp": 120, "deadline": "18:00", "countdown": "2h 14m left",
   "streak_risk": -3, "target_region": "academy"},
]

seeds = [
  {"id": "seed-1", "label": "Morning Routine", "state": "DORMANT",  # DORMANT/GROWING/READY/PLANTED/BLOOMING
   "potential_xp": 80, "potential_attr": "dsc"},
]

judge_reviews = [
  {"id": 42, "task": "Study Control Systems", "status": "COMPLETED_LATE",
   "user_reason": "Unexpected assignment from another class.",
   "metrics": {"validity": 82, "responsibility": 71, "consistency": 94},
   "penalty": -12, "discipline_delta": 0, "review_status": "PENDING"},
]

activity = [
  {"name": "Meditate", "completed_at": "21:04", "xp": 25, "attr": "fcs", "attr_delta": 1, "target_region": "moon"},
]

world_events = [
  {"headline": "ACADEMY BLOSSOMED", "body": "INT reached 80. A new library has appeared."},
]
```

Region **tier**, computed server-side only, never in JS/templates: `value 0–39 → tier 1`, `40–59 → tier 2`, `60–79 → tier 3`, `80–100 → tier 4`.

---

## Stage 0 — Asset placeholder system (build this before anything that uses an image)

**Goal:** the page always renders something clean and legible, whether real art exists, partial art exists, or zero art exists.

The full list of expected external files (filenames, folders, dimensions) is in the companion file `garden-image-generation-brief.md` — do not duplicate that spec here, just consume the filenames it defines.

### Server-side existence check (primary mechanism)

Write one helper, called once per request when building the context dict:

```python
import os

def asset_exists(relative_static_path):
    full_path = os.path.join(app.static_folder, relative_static_path)
    return os.path.exists(full_path)
```

For every image the theme references, compute a boolean alongside its path and pass both into the template — never let the template guess:

```python
def region_art(region_key, tier):
    rel_path = f"img/regions/{region_key}-tier{tier}.png"
    return {"path": rel_path, "exists": asset_exists(rel_path)}

def hero_bg(season):
    rel_path = f"img/garden-hero-{season.lower()}.jpg"
    return {"path": rel_path, "exists": asset_exists(rel_path)}

def health_overlay(state):
    filename = {"FLOURISHING": "garden-health-flourishing.png",
                "STABLE": "garden-health-stable.png",
                "NEGLECTED": "garden-health-neglected.png"}[state]
    rel_path = f"img/{filename}"
    return {"path": rel_path, "exists": asset_exists(rel_path)}
```

Attach these computed dicts to the context: `regions.academy.art = region_art("academy", regions.academy.tier)`, `hero_bg_data = hero_bg(player.season)`, `health_overlay_data = health_overlay(garden_health.state)`.

### Template branching (every image tag follows this exact pattern, no exceptions)

```html
{% if hero_bg_data.exists %}
  <img src="{{ url_for('static', filename=hero_bg_data.path) }}" class="grpg-hero-bg" alt="">
{% else %}
  <div class="grpg-hero-bg grpg-placeholder-hero"></div>
{% endif %}
```

```html
{% if regions.academy.art.exists %}
  <img src="{{ url_for('static', filename=regions.academy.art.path) }}" class="grpg-region-art" alt="">
{% else %}
  <div class="grpg-region-art grpg-placeholder-region" style="--placeholder-color: var(--accent-int);">
    <span class="grpg-placeholder-label">ACADEMY · T{{ regions.academy.tier }}</span>
  </div>
{% endif %}
```

Same `{% if %}/{% else %}` pattern for every one of the 4 region overlays and the health overlay. The health overlay's `{% else %}` branch renders nothing at all (an empty/absent element) rather than a placeholder box, since a missing mood-tint is supposed to be invisible by design (this matches `garden-health-stable.png` being intentionally blank).

### Placeholder CSS (write these once, reused everywhere)

```css
[data-theme="garden-rpg"] .grpg-placeholder-hero {
  width: 100%; height: 100%;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #5B2A6E 0%, #C4416B 40%, #E86A3B 75%, #F4A93C 100%);
}

[data-theme="garden-rpg"] .grpg-placeholder-region {
  width: 100%; height: 100%;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  border: 1.5px dashed var(--placeholder-color);
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--placeholder-color) 15%, transparent);
}

[data-theme="garden-rpg"] .grpg-placeholder-label {
  font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: var(--placeholder-color); text-align: center; padding: 4px;
}
```

The gradient in `.grpg-placeholder-hero` uses the exact same 4-stop color values specified in the image brief, so even the fallback stays on-brand instead of looking broken. The dashed circle placeholder for regions clearly signals "art not generated yet" without looking like an error state — it should look intentional, like a design-system empty state, not a broken image icon.

### Client-side defense-in-depth (secondary, cheap insurance)

In addition to the server-side check, add `onerror` handlers to every real `<img>` tag as a backup in case a file exists at build time but fails to load at request time (permissions, partial upload, etc.):

```html
<img src="..." class="grpg-hero-bg" alt=""
     onerror="this.outerHTML='<div class=&quot;grpg-hero-bg grpg-placeholder-hero&quot;></div>';">
```

This is a safety net only — the server-side `{% if exists %}` check in Stage 0 is the real mechanism and should handle the vast majority of cases. Do not rely on `onerror` alone.

**Done when:** deleting every file in `static/img/` and `static/img/regions/` and reloading the page shows a fully-formed, legible layout with dashed-circle placeholders and a gradient hero background — nothing broken, no missing-image icons, no layout shift compared to when real art is present.

## Stage 1 — The garden becomes stateful (highest priority)

**Goal:** regions visibly reflect their attribute's tier.

- In `_hero_garden.html`, select the seasonal hero file and each region's tier file server-side (Stage 0's helpers), rendering through the `{% if exists %}` pattern every time. Because Jinja renders the correct tier's path server-side, no client-side tier-switching logic is needed — nothing to implement in JS for the static render.
- Position each region element (real image OR placeholder div, both use the same `.grpg-region-art` class so positioning CSS applies identically either way) centered on its anchor point:

| Region | top % | left % |
|---|---|---|
| Academy | 32% | 46% |
| River | 48% | 22% |
| Moon | 45% | 76% |
| Village | 68% | 58% |

  via `style="top: 32%; left: 46%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);"` (one specific value per region, not shared).
- Stacking order: `z-index: 1` on `.grpg-hero-bg`, `z-index: 2` on the health overlay, `z-index: 3` on every `.grpg-region-art`, `z-index: 4` on the quote/badge/Petals/Seeds UI cards.
- DSC does not get a region. It drives `garden_health.state` only, rendered as the Stage 0 health-overlay image/absence.
- Each region's badge (the small pill, e.g. "ACADEMY · INT 72") gets exactly these CSS states: default = `box-shadow: 0 0 8px 0 var(--badge-color);`; `:hover` = `box-shadow: 0 0 14px 2px var(--badge-color);`; `.grpg-region-selected` (added by JS on click, removed when a different region is clicked) = an expanded info panel appears beneath it showing that attribute's 3 most recent `activity` entries where `target_region` matches; `.grpg-region-pulse` (added by JS for exactly 2000ms then removed via `setTimeout`, triggered when that region's `tier` changes between two data refreshes) = `animation: grpg-pulse 2s ease-out 1;`, keyframes scaling the box-shadow from `0 0 8px` up to `0 0 24px 6px var(--badge-color)` and back down.

**Done when:** changing a region's `tier` value in the data changes which art (or placeholder) renders, without touching markup structure; DSC changes the whole garden's mood, not a 5th region; the page passes Stage 0's "delete all images" test with this markup in place.

## Stage 2 — Fix navigation (resolve top/bottom duplication)

**Goal:** one nav hierarchy, not two competing ones.

- Bottom nav is the ONLY primary navigation: `HOME · MISSIONS · GARDEN · STATS · JOURNAL · INVENTORY · SHOP`, icon + label on every item, per the base theme guide's Section 10.
- Remove "Today" from the top bar. Home *is* today. Remaining top-bar icons (Map, Journal-shortcut, Stats-shortcut) are secondary/contextual only — smaller, muted, no active-state pill, must not visually compete with the bottom nav.
- Rebuild the icon set from one consistent thin-line SVG icon set (reuse whatever icon system the base project already has if one exists; add exactly one new sprite set only if it doesn't). Icon-to-label mapping:
  - Home → shrine/torii glyph
  - Missions → crossed blades or scroll
  - Garden → flower/bonsai
  - Stats → bar graph
  - Journal → open book
  - Inventory → chest/bag
  - Shop → merchant stall

**Done when:** exactly one place on the page reads as "the nav"; no icon is an emoji or a mismatched style from the rest.

## Stage 3 — Mission depth

**Goal:** missions carry real RPG information.

- Collapsed mission row adds: difficulty dots (●●●○○ from `difficulty`), and a small colored dot per attribute key present in `attr_deltas`.
- Clicking a mission row toggles a `.grpg-mission-expanded` class (JS), height transitions via CSS `grid-template-rows` (no animation library), revealing: attribute deltas listed individually (e.g. "INT +3 · FCS +1 · DSC +1"), difficulty, deadline + countdown, reward XP, streak risk, and three buttons — `[START MISSION]` `[RESCHEDULE]` `[ABANDON]`.
- Render every value in the `status` enum with a distinct style: AVAILABLE (muted outline), ACTIVE (attribute-colored outline), COMPLETED (white/gold check — not green, see Stage 6), COMPLETED_LATE (amber), MISSED (red outline, no fill), ABANDONED (red, muted), RESCHEDULED (grey, clock icon), LOCKED (low-opacity, lock icon).
- Add a "Current Objective" block above the mission list (or pinned near the hero) surfacing the single highest-priority ACTIVE mission with a compact reward/deadline preview and a `[START MISSION]` button.
- Optional: an "Optimal Route" mini-panel listing 2-3 missions in suggested order with a combined expected-reward summary.

**Done when:** every value in the expanded `status` enum has a visually distinct treatment; clicking any mission reveals the full detail card without leaving Home.

## Stage 4 — System Judge becomes a real review system

**Goal:** the Judge explains itself and keeps history.

- Expand the review card to show: numbered review (`REVIEW #{{ review.id }}`), task, status, user's submitted reason if any, the three assessment metrics as bars, penalty, discipline delta, and `[ACCEPT]` / `[DISPUTE]` buttons that update `review_status`.
- Add a review history list (own scrollable section, or a dedicated `templates/judge_log.html` route linked from "View Log") — each past review as a compact row: id, task, status word (Accepted/Disputed/Pending/Overturned), penalty.

**Done when:** the Judge panel shows *why* a penalty was applied, and more than one review is visible somewhere.

---

## Stage 5 — Visual hierarchy

**Goal:** clear tiering, not "10 equal cards."

- **Tier 1** (largest visual presence): hero garden + Current Objective block.
- **Tier 2**: Level/XP block, Attributes panel, Streak.
- **Tier 3**: Garden Status, System Judge, Discipline.
- **Tier 4** (smallest, most muted): XP Flow, Recent Activity, secondary analytics.
- Implement via `box-shadow` intensity, border opacity, and panel padding — Tier 1 gets no hard rectangular border (soft vignette/gradient edge instead), Tier 4 panels get thinner padding and more `--text-secondary`-forward typography.
- Shrink the Petals/Seeds overlay cards and/or increase their background transparency so more of the garden art is visible at once — they should feel anchored to the world, not covering most of it.

**Done when:** at a glance, the garden + current objective are unmistakably first; the analytics row reads as secondary.

---

## Stage 6 — Color semantics, formalized

| Attribute | Primary (HUD) | World cue |
|---|---|---|
| INT | cyan `--accent-int` | ivory/soft-blue lantern glow at Academy |
| STA | red/orange `--accent-sta` | teal/water-blue accents at River |
| FCS | gold `--accent-fcs` | deep indigo/violet moonlight at Moon |
| CHA | purple `--accent-cha` | warm violet lantern/flowers at Village |
| DSC | green `--accent-dsc` | overall garden health treatment (Stage 1), not a location |

Rules:
- Green appears ONLY on DSC-related UI (the Discipline card, DSC bars/deltas). Nowhere else.
- "Completion" states (mission done, activity logged) use white or soft gold, never green, unless the completed thing is specifically a DSC action.
- Penalties use a subdued red on the specific value only — never tint the whole panel red.
- Add `--accent-active`, a neutral cyan/white token reserved for "currently active/selected" (active mission, selected region, current nav item, focus mode) — kept separate from the 5 attribute colors so "active" and "this is an INT thing" never look coincidentally identical.

**Done when:** grep the CSS for green usage and confirm it only touches discipline-related elements.

---

## Stage 7 — Living-world feedback loop

**Goal:** completing something visibly travels from task → attribute → world.

- On mission/petal completion (extend `initMissionToggles`/`initPetalsToggles`): show a brief inline summary before collapsing the row — XP gained, each attribute delta, and a line like `→ Academy` naming `target_region` — then trigger that region's `.grpg-region-pulse` class for ~2s.
- Recent Activity rows show the same shape: name, `completed_at`, XP, attribute delta, `→ {target_region}` — not just a checkmark and a number.
- World Events: a small dismissible `.grpg-world-event` banner rendered whenever a region's computed tier increases between renders — headline + one-line body from `world_events`. Generate these server-side when tier crosses a threshold, not ad hoc in JS.
- Seasonal/time-of-day theming already flows through Stage 0/1's `hero_bg` selection by `player.season`; drive the existing day/night toggle's overlay intensity from `player.time_of_day` instead of leaving it purely decorative.

**Done when:** completing a mission in the demo produces a visible, readable chain (task → XP/attribute line → region pulse) before settling back to the static state.

---

## Stage 8 — Analytics depth (its own page, not Home)

Home keeps only XP Flow (7-day bars) and Discipline summary. Everything else moves to `templates/stats.html`, reachable from the bottom nav's Stats item: attribute history (7/30/90-day toggle), attribute heatmap, mission completion breakdown (on-time/late/missed %), streak history (current/best/worst + calendar-heatmap strip), habit consistency, time distribution, penalty history. Reuse `.grpg-panel` styles — denser grid of the same visual language, not a new design system.

**Done when:** Stats in the bottom nav lands on a page with all of the above; Home doesn't try to cram in more than XP Flow + Discipline summary.

---

## Stage 9 — Player identity and world ownership

- Add `player.garden_name` as a small serif label integrated near the quote block in the hero (not another floating card): "Kim's Garden · Day 42 · Spring."
- Expand the Wayfarer bottom-row card: current title, next title, streak count, a "recent growth" line (e.g. "+2 INT · +1 STA") from the last 24-48h of `activity`.
- Make the avatar clickable → `templates/profile.html`: title, level, achievements list, read-only garden state view. Minimal is fine, it just needs to be a real destination.
- Journal (bottom nav item): let an entry optionally tag an attribute (`journal_entry.linked_attr` in the data model), even if the full linking-to-world-growth logic isn't built yet — the field needs to exist so Stage 7's world-event generator can consume it later.

**Done when:** a first-time viewer can identify whose garden this is without a tooltip; the avatar is a real link.

---

## Stage 10 — Atmosphere and polish (last)

- Small looping ambient details on the hero: a handful of `.grpg-petal` divs with a slow CSS `@keyframes` drift/fall animation (`pointer-events: none`), a soft firefly glow near Moon, gentle water shimmer on River (CSS gradient animation, not physics). Wrap all of it in `@media (not (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce))`.
- Border treatment variation: normal panel = subtle grey border; active mission/selected region = attribute-colored border; warning = subtle amber/red; achievement = gold; locked = low-opacity grey. Audit every panel.
- Optional Focus Mode: a `.grpg-focus-active` toggle class on `.grpg-dashboard` that dims/hides side panels via `opacity` + `pointer-events:none`, darkens the hero overlay, and shows a countdown timer for the active mission. Build only after Stages 1-9 are solid.

**Done when:** the page feels alive at a glance without being distracting; reduced-motion users get a fully static equivalent.
